h1: English language requirement for UK visas
intro: The English language requirement depends on your visa. Here are the levels for each route, the ways to prove your English, and who is exempt.
cardText: The level you need for each route, and how to prove it.

sections.heading: English language requirement by route
sections.text:
- Spouse or partner visa: A1 for a first application, A2 to extend, B1 for settlement
- Skilled Worker visa: B2 for new applicants since January 2026
- Student visa: usually B2 for degree-level study
- Indefinite Leave to Remain and British citizenship: B1, with higher levels planned for ILR under the new rules

sections.heading: How to prove your English
sections.text: By passing a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from an approved provider at the right level, by having a degree taught in English (confirmed by Ecctis if from outside the UK), or by being a national of a majority English-speaking country.

sections.heading: Who is exempt?
sections.text: People aged 65 or over, people with a long-term physical or mental condition that prevents them meeting the requirement, and nationals of majority English-speaking countries are usually exempt. The exemptions differ by route.

faqs.q: Which English test should I take?
faqs.a: A SELT from a Home Office approved provider, at the level your route requires. Tests from other providers aren’t accepted.

faqs.q: Does my degree meet the English language requirement?
faqs.a: A degree taught in English can, with confirmation from Ecctis if it’s from outside the UK.

faqs.q: How long is an English test valid for?
faqs.a: Usually 2 years from the test date, though passes used in earlier successful applications can sometimes be reused.

title: English Language Requirement for UK Visas | 2026 Guide
description: The English language requirement for UK visas: levels for spouse, Skilled Worker, student, ILR and citizenship, approved tests and exemptions.
